The result must be stated as supporting or disfavoring at least one named hypothesis (H1 no braking action in held input; H2 braking commanded but speed not reduced; H3 braking infeasible under the 8.0 N limits), not as a root cause.

If the saved state or held input needed for the probe is not retained or not computable, the check must return an explicit not-retained / not-computable status instead of an inferred cause.

hypotheses: H1_no_braking_action_in_held_input: at the terminal update 34 the recorded held tension contains no braking box action (e.g., the one channel with tension ~1.42e-08 N is effectively slack and no channel opposes the residual tip motion), so residual tip speed persists because the terminal objective/plan never commands deceleration - consistent with negligible terminal_tip_speed_weight/holding_tip_speed_weight and a 0.1 s horizon.

H2_braking_commanded_but_projected_speed_not_reduced: a braking box solution does differ from the recorded held tension, yet the one-step projected tip speed under the held input is not materially reduced over the 0.01 s probe, which would point to commanded-but-ineffective authority (actuation/passive or model mismatch) rather than to objective weighting.

H3_braking_requires_tension_infeasible_under_limits: the braking box solution saturates one or more channels at the 8.0 N force limits (reference 0a960268cc836ca9e5c5871afcad116033e0bd22471092179506f2efd9c580cd, /tendons/0..5/force_limit_n = 8.0), so residual motion is not attributable to the weighting scheme alone but to per-channel force limits within the probe step.
